claim: Tower of London 2026 online adult tickets start around £34.80 (gate £39.80), child (5-15) £18.50, senior £29.50, with advance booking strongly recommended as slots sell out.
quote: Online prices start from £37 for adults, £18.50 for children (5–15), and £29.50 for seniors (65+). Adult admission costs £34.80 when booked online... gate prices increasing to £39.80

claim: Buckingham Palace State Rooms 2026 summer opening runs 9 July to 27 September, daily 9:30am-7:30pm through August 31 then Thu-Mon 9:30am-6:30pm in September.
quote: The State Rooms are open from 9 July to 27 September 2026. July 9 to August 31: open daily, 9:30 a.m. to 7:30 p.m. From September 1 to September 27, the palace shifts to Thursday through Monday only, from 9:30 a.m. to 6:30 p.m.

claim: Buckingham Palace 2026 tickets are £33 adult (25+), £21.50 (18-24), £16.50 child (5+); same-day tickets cost £2-4 extra and 19 State Rooms plus garden access typically need 2-3 hours.
quote: Adults (25+): £33... Ages 18-24: £21.50... Children 5+: £16.50... Advance booking is recommended, as same-day purchases cost an extra £2-4 and often sell out... Visitors access 19 State Rooms... two to three hours.

claim: Westminster Abbey 2026 adult admission is £31 (£28 senior/student, £14 child 6-17, under 5 free) with multimedia guide included; open Mon-Sat with hours varying by day, closed Sundays for tourism.
quote: Adults: £31... Adults 65+ and students: £28... Children (6-17 years): £14... A multimedia guide is included with admission... The Abbey is a working church and sometimes subject to closure at short notice.

claim: St Paul's Cathedral 2026 sightseeing tickets are £27 adult, £24 senior/student, £10.50 child, £64.50 family (2A+2-3C), including Cathedral Floor, Crypt, Dome Galleries and multimedia guide.
quote: Adults (18+): £27... Seniors (65+) and Students: £24... Children (6-17 years): £10.50... admission includes entry to the Cathedral Floor, Crypt and the Dome Galleries plus multimedia guides.

claim: UK Parliament 2026 guided tours cost £34 adult, £28 young adult (16-24), £18 child (5-15); self-guided multimedia tours are £27/£20/£10 and a Speaker's House tour runs £21.
quote: The guided tour costs £34 for adults, £28 for young adults (16-24), £18 for children (5-15)... Self-Guided Audio Tours (Multimedia) Adults £27, Young adults (16-24) £20, Children (5-15) £10.

claim: Tower Bridge Exhibition 2026 is open daily 9:30am-6pm (last entry 5pm) covering North/South Towers, glass-floor high-level walkways and Victorian Engine Rooms, bookable up to 8 weeks ahead.
quote: Tower Bridge is open daily from 9:30 AM to 6:00 PM, with last entry at 5:00 PM... Entry to Tower Bridge includes access to the North and South Towers, High-Level Walkways, and Engine Rooms, and can be booked up to 8 weeks in advance.

claim: London Eye 2026 standard adult tickets start ~£29-33 online (Fast Track £44-49), with prices dynamic and lower the further ahead you book; one rotation lasts ~30 minutes in shared 25-person glass capsules.
quote: Standard tickets start from approximately £29–£33 per adult (online, varies by date and demand), and Fast Track tickets start from approximately £44–£49. Prices are dynamic — the earlier you book, the lower the price.

claim: Sky Garden offers free timed-entry tickets booked in advance through tickets.skygarden.london, with the venue itself open Mon-Thu 8am-midnight, Fri/Sat 8am-1am, Sun 8am-midnight.
quote: Monday-Thursday: 8am-12am (midnight)... Friday & Saturday: 8am-1am... Sunday: 8am-12am... Sky Garden provides 'free ticket' access to the garden itself.

claim: Lift 109 (the glass chimney lift at Battersea Power Station) sells off-peak from £17, standard from £19.75 and peak from £21.45, with child tickets from £12.60 and under-3s free, for a sub-1-hour 109-metre 360° view experience.
quote: The Chimney Lift offers three pricing tiers: Off Peak from £17.00, Standard from £19.75, and Peak from £21.45... adult tickets start from £17, with children's tickets from £12.60. Additionally, infants under 3 go free.

claim: Experienced traveller verdict: Tower of London (with Yeomen Warder tour, 2+ hours) is highly worth it, the London Eye divides on weather and long queues, while Sky Garden's outdoor platform is often closed and crowded — Garden at 120 is a better free alternative.
quote: Tower of London... the London tourist attraction I have visited the most often... London Eye... the views really are spectacular (as long as you hit a good-weather day) but... lines can get absolutely insane... Sky Garden... the space was still packed, and the small outdoor observation platform was closed.

claim: St Paul's Cathedral opens to sightseers from 8:30am Mon/Tue/Thu/Fri/Sat (10am Wed) with last sightseeing entry 4pm and Dome Galleries closing at 4:15pm last entry; Sunday Dome access available 15 March-25 October 2026 only.
quote: St Paul's Cathedral doors open at 8.30am on Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, Friday and Saturday, and 10am on Wednesdays, with last entry for sightseeing usually at 4pm. The Dome Galleries open at 9.30am (10am on Wednesdays) with last entry at 4.15pm.
